rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods / Results - authors ran HidroMORE (Sentinel-2 NDVI, FAO56, soil and weather inputs) for the whole olive area of Medenine 2016-2019 and collected gravimetric soil moisture at four sites. Q2: Validation results, Table 2 - model soil water content compared with in situ measurements (overall R2 0.73, IA 0.77); Simulation results, Figs 5-8 - spatial distribution of depletion and stress coefficient by zone, inner plain and coast most affected, mountain/piedmont less stressed due to Jessour/Tabia; Conclusions - study offers an objective tool to prioritise orchards for intervention. Q4: Model description Eq. 3-7 and Figs 7A-B - soil water depletion and stress coefficient Ks (the intermediate variables linking RS inputs to drought stress) are simulated, and soil water content is measured in situ. Q5: Table 2 and Figs 7-8 - results reported separately for four agro-ecological zones (mountain Zammour, piedmont Ksar Jedid, inner plain Dar Dhaoui, coast Zarzis) with different climate and soils. Q6: Model simulation section - simulation covers the entire olive land use of the governorate (8588 km2, ~200,000 ha olives), results given by region. Q7: Discussion (model evaluation) - a finer soil map with better soil characteristics is stated as crucial to improve simulation results; better results where soil parameters came from field/lab data; denser weather station network needed to avoid mis-represented rainfall. Q8: Discussion - persistent overestimation of soil water content, weak correlation in coastal and inner plain sites, root depth and within-zone variability underestimated, coarse 1/200,000 soil map, FAO56 underestimates ET, no horizontal runoff between pixels, no 2018 soil moisture data.
rows.notes: The study maps drought stress with a RS-based water balance validated against soil moisture; actual prioritisation of interventions is proposed as a use, not demonstrated through an applied intervention. Q3: the stress maps come from the model alone; in situ soil moisture serves as validation at four points, not an independent second method establishing the mapped stress. Q9: Table 2 gives min, max, standard deviation and RMSE of the soil water content comparison, but no dispersion measure for the drought stress/depletion maps that constitute the claimed result; RMSE does not count, so rated no with doubt.

notes: Full text available; figures referenced but not reproduced.
